issues.description: Test fixtures show `fix.text: '0deg'` where the inserted string should be `'deg'` — verify it isn't a copy-paste artifact.
issues.detail: Multiple reject cases declare `fix.text` as `'0deg'` over a range that only spans the position after the number, while the `fixed` output ends in `'10deg'`/`'1deg'`. Pike and Torvalds both flagged this as suspicious. Confirm the test harness semantics (insertion vs. replacement) or correct the literal before it masks a real fixer bug.

issues.description: `0 + offset` is dead arithmetic; write `args[offset]` (or a named `HUE_INDEX + offset`).
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged `args[0 + offset]` as noise. Replace with `args[offset]`, or introduce a named constant so the positional invariant reads itself. Trivial cleanup but the patch is small enough that every line should earn its place.

issues.description: Positional invariant on `args` (from, source, channels...) is load-bearing but uncommented.
issues.detail: The fix relies on the invariant that after filtering to word/function nodes, position 0 is `from`, position 1 is the source color, and positions 2..N are the channels. A one-line comment naming the positions — or a small `{funcName: hueIndex}` table plus `relativeOffset(args)` helper — would let a reader verify correctness without running tests and survive future filter refactors.

issues.description: Missing reject-case coverage for nested relative-color where the outer hue needs fixing.
issues.detail: Accept tests cover `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)`, but no reject case exercises an outer function whose hue needs the fix while the `from` source is itself a function. Add one test to lock in that the `args[0]?.value` lookup doesn't get fooled by a function-typed first arg.

issues.description: Test corpus omits `none` keyword (and `calc()`) as channel values in relative-color position.
issues.detail: Relative color syntax permits `none` and `calc(...)` as channel values (e.g. `oklch(from red l c none)`). Added tests cover identifiers and numbers but not these. Cheap to add and prevents the next bug report from surprising anyone.

synthesis.summary: The panel accepts the patch. It is small, local, and algorithmically correct: detect `from` as the first arg and shift the channel index by 2. Complexity is unchanged and the data shape drives the algorithm cleanly. The main concern shared by Pike and Torvalds is a suspicious `fix.text: '0deg'` literal in the new reject fixtures that warrants verification. Beyond that, trivial cleanups — drop `0 + offset`, name the positional invariant, and extend tests to cover nested relative-color reject cases and the `none` keyword.
